items.title: The State of AEO/GEO in 2026: CMO Investment Report
items.summary: 94% of enterprises plan to increase investments in AEO/GEO in 2026, according to a survey of more than 250 executives and digital decision-makers conducted by Conductor. The report reveals budget benchmarks, resourcing strategies, and content approaches that differentiate leading brands in AI search visibility. Key impacts include a shift toward in-house capabilities, focus on data quality, and new KPIs like conversions and AI search market share.

items.title: New SEO Fundamentals: Mastering AEO, GEO, SXO, and ACO
items.summary: Traditional SEO is losing ground to AI-driven search, where small brands can compete by focusing on AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), GEO (Generative Engine Optimization), SXO, and ACO. AI prioritizes entity authority, structured data, and topical relevance over domain authority and backlinks. Tools like Pierview.ai help track AI citations and outperform competitors in this new frontier.

items.title: Entering the Era of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
items.summary: SEO is evolving into GEO, where search engines generate answers using platforms like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews instead of traditional blue links. Success requires structuring content for AI to understand, trust, extract, and cite it, emphasizing topical authority, machine-readable formats, and expertise. Brands must optimize for inclusion in AI responses rather than just SERP rankings.

items.title: Thousands of authors publish 'empty' book 'Don't Steal This Book' to protest AI at London Book Fair
items.summary: Over 10,000 authors including Kazuo Ishiguro, Philippa Gregory, and Richard Osman released an empty book titled 'Don't Steal This Book' at the London Book Fair to protest AI companies using their work without consent for training. The protest visualizes concerns over copyright infringement in AI development. It coincides with discussions on AI's impact on creative industries.

items.title: Should Writers Still Chase Big 5 Traditional Publishing in 2026?
items.summary: Traditional Big 5 publishing faces criticism for long timelines, low sales under 1000 copies, and unearned advances, making it viable mainly for specific demographics writing BookTok-friendly novels. Publishers chase BookTok hits like Alchemized which sold millions, sidelining others. Indie publishing allows direct reader access and success without gatekeepers.

items.title: Korean publisher Luminary Books floods market with 9,000 AI-generated titles in one year
items.summary: Luminary Books released about 9,000 titles in 2025 at an unthinkable pace reliant on extensive AI use, sparking controversy in Korea's publishing industry. The AI-generated books are flooding shelves, raising ethical questions. Industry watchers highlight the rapid proliferation enabled by AI.

items.title: Big publishers using AI forecasting models to predict book hits and decide promotions
items.summary: Major publishers are developing AI models to forecast which books will succeed, determining purchases and promotions. Author Ewan Morrison warns of dark times ahead for literature as AI takes control. He notes a past satirical prediction is now reality.

items.title: Publishers ideologically captured, relying on BookTok indie hits to survive
items.summary: Traditional publishers depend on TikTok/BookTok indie successes after failing with progressive titles, forcing acquisition of self-published hits. Barnes & Noble shelves filled with ex-indie BookTok books earning seven figures pre-deal. Author calls for patrons supporting soulful, genre-building work over fast tropes.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Addresses Backlash to 'Woke' Snow White Reboot
items.summary: Rachel Zegler slammed the backlash she received for her casting and comments on Disney's Snow White reboot, vowing she refuses to assimilate for others' comfort after the film's box office flop. Disney reportedly scaled back promotion anticipating anti-woke audience reaction. The controversy highlights changes to the classic story perceived as preachy by viewers.

items.title: James Gunn Slams 'Woke' Backlash Over Superman Themes
items.summary: Superman director James Gunn hit back at Fox News and conservative critics labeling his upcoming film 'woke' due to its themes. The backlash comes amid high anticipation for the DC reboot. Gunn defended the movie's direction against claims of preachiness.

items.title: Pixar Cuts LGBTQ Storyline from 'Elio' Amid Creative Overhaul
items.summary: Pixar chief Pete Docter explained removing queer themes from 'Elio' after director change and poor testing, stating 'we're making a movie, not therapy.' The decision follows audience feedback and reflects caution around potentially preachy content. The film is set for 2025 release post-revisions.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Faces Backlash Over Ballet Comments Ahead of Oscars
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet drew ire for remarking 'no one cares' about ballet or opera, deepening controversy as an Oscar nominee for Marty Supreme. Despite celebrity defenses, fans and critics highlighted perceived dismissiveness. The drama adds to pre-Oscars buzz.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Snow White Backlash Shared Widely on X
items.summary: Users on X reposted news of Rachel Zegler's response to backlash over the 'woke' Snow White remake following its poor performance. Discussions focused on Disney's changes and audience rejection of altered narrative. Post garnered attention amid ongoing culture debates.

items.title: Catturd Calls for Oscar Boycott Amid Perceived Woke Shift
items.summary: Influencer Catturd announced a 'great day not to watch the Oscars,' reflecting audience sentiment against the ceremony's direction. Replies echoed backlash to Hollywood's preachy elements. Post highlights growing disinterest in awards shows.

items.title: 5 AI Tools to Run a 1-Person Business While You Sleep
items.summary: This article outlines five powerful AI tools designed to automate operations for solo entrepreneurs, allowing businesses to run passively even while the owner sleeps. Highlighted by Entrepreneur contributors, these tools focus on practical automation for small-scale operations. They represent new AI solutions that deliver real efficiency gains for one-person businesses.

items.title: PosterMyWall AI Brings Prompt-Driven Marketing Campaigns to Small Businesses
items.summary: PosterMyWall has launched a new AI tool that enables small businesses to create entire marketing campaigns from a single prompt, handling everything from ideation to publication within one app. Unlike standalone image generators, it streamlines the full process for non-technical users. This product move makes advanced marketing accessible and efficient for SMBs.

items.title: Small Business Owners Quietly Building Custom AI Solutions for Massive Savings
items.summary: Small business owners are leveraging AI to build custom tools like an AI receptionist for dentists saving $4k/month, demand predictors for food trucks cutting waste by 40%, style-matching editors for photographers doubling bookings, churn predictors boosting gym retention 22%, and bespoke CRMs replacing costly software. These real-world examples highlight the tangible impact of AI on operations without needing professional coders. The post warns of the growing gap between AI builders and those merely observing.

items.title: AI Forces Redesign of Business Work Structures and Authority
items.summary: AI is breaking down traditional boundaries between business functions like IT, analytics, product, and operations, shifting authority and requiring new operating models. Leaders risk creating isolated AI roles without integrating them into scalable enterprise capabilities. The post argues that success lies in redesigning work around AI, not just adding titles.
